subject: spanish

questions.q: What does “el sueldo” mean?
questions.explain: “El sueldo” means “the salary/wage”; “el suelo” (floor) is a near-miss distractor.

questions.q: What does “aprobar un examen” mean?
questions.explain: “Aprobar” means “to pass”; to fail is “suspender”.

questions.q: What does 'el desempleo' mean?
questions.explain: 'El desempleo' (also 'el paro') means 'unemployment'; 'el empleo' is 'employment/a job'.

questions.q: Which sentence means “I would like to work abroad in the future”?
options: Me gustaría trabajo en el extranjero en el futuro
Me gustaría trabajar en el extranjero en el pasado
Me gusta trabajar en el extranjero en el futuro
Me gustaría trabajar en el extranjero en el futuro
questions.explain: “En el futuro” = in the future and “trabajar en el extranjero” = work abroad; “me gustaría” is the conditional.

questions.q: What does “es comprensivo” mean?
questions.explain: “Comprensivo” means “understanding”, not “comprehensive”.

questions.q: How do you say “Smoking damages your health”?
questions.explain: “Fumar” = to smoke and “perjudicar la salud” = to damage your health.

questions.q: What does 'el billete de ida y vuelta' mean?
questions.explain: 'Ida y vuelta' means 'there and back', so 'el billete de ida y vuelta' = 'a return ticket'.

questions.q: What does 'mi hermano mayor' mean?
questions.explain: 'Mayor' means 'older/elder', so 'mi hermano mayor' = 'my older brother'. 'Menor' would mean younger.

questions.q: How do you say 'I get on well with my sister'?
options: Me llevo bien con mi hermana
questions.explain: 'Llevarse bien con' means 'to get on well with', so 'Me llevo bien con mi hermana' = 'I get on well with my sister'.

questions.q: Which sentence means “I work as a waiter at the weekend”?
options: Trabajo de camarero los fines de semana
Trabajo de cartero los fines de semana
Trabaja de camarero los fines de semana
questions.explain: “De camarero” = as a waiter and “los fines de semana” = at the weekend.

questions.q: What does “el director” mean in a school context?
questions.explain: At school “el director” means “the headteacher/principal”.

questions.q: How do you say “You should drink plenty of water”?
questions.explain: “Se debe” = “one should” and “beber” (not “comer”) is used for drinks: “Se debe beber mucha agua”.

questions.q: How do you say “I have a headache”?
questions.explain: “Me duele la cabeza” = “my head hurts / I have a headache”.

questions.q: What does “la muela” mean?
questions.explain: “La muela” means a “molar/back tooth”, so “me duele la muela” = toothache.

questions.q: Which means “The pay is low but I enjoy the work”?
options: El suelo es bajo pero disfruto del trabajo
El sueldo es bajo pero odio el trabajo
El sueldo es bajo pero disfruto del trabajo
El sueldo es alto pero disfruto del trabajo
questions.explain: “El sueldo es bajo” = the pay is low and “disfruto del trabajo” = I enjoy the work.

questions.q: What does 'el aprobado' mean?
questions.explain: 'Aprobar' means 'to pass', so 'el aprobado' is a pass grade. A fail is 'el suspenso'.

questions.q: What does “hacer footing” mean?
questions.explain: “Hacer footing” is a borrowed term meaning “to go jogging/running”.

questions.q: How do you say “I work part-time in a shop”?
options: Trabajo a tiempo parcial en una tienda
Trabajo a tiempo parcial en una empresa
Trabajas a tiempo parcial en una tienda
Trabajo a tiempo completo en una tienda
questions.explain: “A tiempo parcial” = part-time and “una tienda” = a shop, so the first option is correct.

questions.q: What does “engordar” mean?
questions.explain: “Engordar” means “to put on weight / get fat”; the opposite is “adelgazar”.

questions.q: How do you say “I get on well with my sister”?
options: Me llevo bien con mi hermana
questions.explain: “Llevarse bien con” means “to get on well with”, so “me llevo bien con mi hermana”.

questions.q: What does “mi medio hermano” mean?
questions.explain: “Medio hermano” means “half-brother” (one shared parent).

questions.q: What does “el aprendizaje” most commonly mean?
questions.explain: “El aprendizaje” means “learning”, and in a work context “an apprenticeship”.
